The Hyper-MUCHFUSS survey aims at finding high-velocity potentially unbound hot subdwarf stars.
three candidates among the sdB stars
The sdB star SDSS J123137.56+074621.7 (J1231) and the He-sdO star SDSS J205030.39−061957.8 (J2050) have been discovered as new objects with extreme kinematics (Geier et al. 2015b).

notes: The three counted stars are the paper’s “three candidates among the sdB stars” and its three sdB targets from Hyper-MUCHFUSS; the later kinematic analysis rejects present-day Galactic unbound status (J1231 bound at 99.9%, T:p7-b12; J1632 “certainly bound,” T:p6-b7; J1644 “must therefore still be bound,” T:p7-b5), but this does not remove follow-up eligibility. The heading/description of J1632 as a “potentially bound HVS” (T:p7-b9, T:p7-b10) is inconsistent with the paper’s earlier definition that HVSs are truly unbound (T:p1-b13); I treated it as a bound/ejected-star label rather than a retained unbound candidacy. J2050 is not counted: it is a spectroscopic twin and possible SN-donor/ejection counterpart, but the paper does not state that it was previously selected as a Galactic unbound candidate and finds it bound at 99.8% (T:p1-b10, T:p7-b13, T:p8-b188). J1644b is only an alternative proper-motion-based solution for J1644, not a separate star (T:p5-b7). US 708 (T:p2-b6) and J1211 (T:p2-b9, T:p4-b6) are cited comparison objects rather than program stars reanalyzed here; US 708 is already unbound, and J1211 is a prior “possibly unbound” comparison.

SDSS J123137.56+074621.7: Multiple catalogue proper-motion determinations in Table 2 (T:p6-b0/I:p6-b0) are retained individually; both the SDSS-BOSS and adopted XSHOOTER radial velocities from Table A.1 (T:p12-b0/I:p12-b0) are retained. No explicit parallax or separate RA/Dec measurements are reported.

SDSS J163213.05+205124.0: For J1632, the T11 proper motion is the one adopted for the kinematic analysis (T:p5-b7; Table 2 at T:p6-b0/I:p6-b0), while the other catalogue proper-motion values in Table 2 are also retained. The adopted radial velocity appears with slightly different uncertainty in Table 1 (-239 ± 4 km/s; T:p4-b0) and Table A.1 for XSHOOTER (-239 ± 2 km/s; T:p12-b0/I:p12-b0); both are recorded rather than choosing one. The paper states that J1632 is “certainly bound” (T:p6-b7) but does not give a numeric bound or unbound probability for J1632 in the supplied material, so no probability value is recorded.

SDSS J164419.44+452326.7: J1644 has discrepant proper motions: the paper treats T11 as the primary J1644 solution and an explicitly unquantified weighted mean of catalogue values as J1644b (T:p5-b7, T:p6-b0). The five catalogue proper-motion pairs are recorded, but the J1644b weighted-mean proper motions themselves are not tabulated. Table A.1 gives multiple radial velocities; Table 1 adopts -309 ± 9 km/s, while Table A.1 also flags the ESI value as adopted for the kinematic calculations (T:p12-b0). I did not include Table 3 velocities at the last disk passage because the velocity quantities are for the present-day state (T:p8-b184); the current v_GRF values are the two quoted in T:p7-b5. No numeric bound/unbound probability for J1644 is explicitly given in the supplied text/table transcription; the paper only states that J1644 "must therefore still be bound" (T:p7-b5).
